title: Null vs Empty String vs Undefined
query: Create a user with name 'John Smith' and no email address

email.description: User's email address (can be null if not provided)

phone.description: Phone number (optional, omit if not provided)

explanation: This tests understanding of NULL vs EMPTY vs UNDEFINED. Email is REQUIRED but allows null (type: ['string', 'null']). User said 'no email' → use null (explicit no value). Don't use empty string '' (that's still a value). Phone is OPTIONAL and not mentioned → OMIT it entirely (undefined). Three states: null (explicit absence), '' (empty but present), undefined (omitted). Check schema types carefully!
learning_points: null = explicitly no value (must be allowed in schema: type: ['string', 'null'])
empty string '' = empty but present (different from null)
undefined = omitted entirely (don't include the key)
If schema says type: ['string', 'null'], you can pass null
If field is optional and not mentioned, omit it (undefined)

wrong_answers.why_wrong: Empty string '' is not the same as null. User has NO email, not an empty one.
email is REQUIRED (in required array), even though it can be null. Must explicitly pass null.
